key_insight: Physics-informed losses only safely enforce constraints that remain closed after coarse-graining; on filtered turbulence, linear constraints survive, while nonlinear PDE residuals can encode the wrong closure.
engineering_relevance: For turbulence surrogates on coarse grids, exact projection onto valid linear constraints can greatly improve stability and conservation at minimal overhead compared with residual penalties or test-time optimization.
method: Train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) on coarse turbulent fields.
Apply a closed-form Fourier-space projection to enforce continuity and global momentum balance exactly.
Optionally model the subgrid flux to close the global energy balance for nonlinear conservation.
evidence_signal: On 2D isotropic turbulence, the projection reduced continuity error to 5.0e-7 and momentum-balance error to 8.6e-11, while raising bounded 448-step rollouts from 0.18 to 0.87; on Kolmogorov flow, test-time optimization was about 3300x more expensive per trajectory.
watch_item: The projection only guarantees constraints that are valid on the filtered grid, so nonlinear physics must be explicitly closed before enforcing them exactly.
paper_title: Only Linear Constraints Survive Coarse-Graining: Evaluating Physics-Constrained Neural Operators on Stochastically Forced Turbulence
